reasoning: The document has excellent text preservation but exhibits significant structural defects. Notably, running headers, footers, and page numbers were improperly retained in the HTML output. Additionally, the heading hierarchy is broken with inconsistent extraction of table titles, and there are minor issues with table splitting and footnote parsing. These structural issues block auto-approval.

concerns.analysis: The table continuation titles ('TABLE 1. - CONTINUED 2011-2012') at the top of several pages are handled inconsistently and improperly. They function as section headings/table titles, but on almost all pages (e.g., Pages 3, 4, 6, 7), they are extracted as plain `<paragraph>` elements instead of headings. Conversely, on Page 5, this exact same text is extracted as a Level 1 Heading. Section headings rendered as plain paragraphs is a defect.

concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=14. Running headers/footers/page numbers should be stripped during PDF-to-HTML conversion.

The source document uses a 6-column layout (two sets of 3 columns placed side-by-side) for its primary tables. Table 1 (spanning multiple pages) and Table 3 (Page 14) are extracted successfully as 6-column tables. However, Table 2 (Page 13) is arbitrarily split into two separate 3-column tables ('1%, 2%, 2.5% and 3% Tax Group' on the left, and 'Lumber & Building Material Group' on the right). This breaks the structural consistency with the source document and the other tables.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: TABLE 2. STATE SALES AND USE TAX... (Single visual 6-column table)
concerns.output_quote: Output splits the single table into two distinct JSON table objects on the same page.

concerns.analysis: The source tables use specific symbols (*, ♠, ♣, ─) to denote footnotes. In the output, the first footnote ('* Gross collections...') on pages 12, 13, and 14 is incorrectly interpreted as an unordered bulleted list item. Because of this parser error, the asterisk character (*) is stripped from the text entirely. This breaks the link between the table header (which still contains the asterisk) and its defining footnote.
